title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: X/S is a smooth relative curve, ω = Ω^1_{X/S} is invertible, and the theme is connections and projective connections on curves. The neighbouring pages are about the local invariant of an order-1 operator (previous page) and the Schwarzian transformation law of c_D (next page).

(1) The crossed-out top line, M_g^φ → M_g, M_{g,c}, looks like a moduli space of curves with extra structure (probably a projective connection) mapping to M_g, with the remark 'net à fibres finies'. It was abandoned.

(2) The P^1-bundle. Set P = P(P^1_{X/S}(ω)), the projectivised bundle of first-order principal parts (1-jets) of ω. Its exact sequence is 0 → Ω⊗ω → P^1(ω) → ω → 0.
- The canonical sub-line gives a distinguished section σ.
- Sections of P disjoint from σ correspond to splittings of the jet sequence ('clivages').
- Splittings correspond to connections on ω, i.e. order-1 differential operators D: ω → ω⊗ω = ω^2 with Leibniz rule D(fα) − fD(α) = α⊗df. In a coordinate, D(f dt) = f D(dt) + dt·df.
- Sections meeting σ correspond to connections on ω with polar singularities. Transverse meeting gives simple poles; higher contact gives higher-order poles.
- He also notes that the 'c' attached to a section shifts to c + ϖ_2 (ϖ_2 ≠ 0) under an action. He asks which actions on P send u(σ) to something of the form c + ϖ_2. This is the torsor structure: projective connections form a torsor under quadratic differentials Γ(ω^2).
- He then wonders whether projective connections can be read as first-order differential data on sections of P, i.e. on connections of ω.

(3) Rank-3 jet/oper picture. He writes a filtered rank-3 bundle 0 ⊂ ω ⊂ L ⊂ V with V⊗ω ≅ ω^2 ⊕ ω ⊕ O as graded pieces. So V has graded pieces ω, O, ω^{-1}, i.e. V is the 2-jet bundle of ω^{-1}, equivalently the adjoint/Sym^2 of the rank-2 sl_2 jet bundle.
- A splitting s: ω^{-1} → V determines a distinguished element v_s ∈ Γ(V⊗ω) with components (0, 0, 1).
- He tries to write a curvature/coefficient c(s) = φ_2 + s⊗φ_1 + v_s·φ_0.
- He changes the splitting by a section of ω, s = s_0 + a_1 with a_1 ∈ Γ(ω), acting by a unipotent gauge transformation exp(θ_{a_1}). The aim is to reduce c(s) to a normal form φ_2 + s_0φ_1 + φ_0 where only the quadratic-differential part φ_2 is free.
- This is the gauge-fixing (Drinfeld–Sokolov-type) description of a projective connection as an sl_2-oper. The next page checks the classical cocycle: c_{D_s} = c_{D_t} + (3s''^2 − 2s's''')/s'^2 dt^2, which is −2 × (Schwarzian derivative), with invariance exactly under homographies.

Overall, the page develops a coordinate-free, scheme-theoretic definition of projective connections on a relative curve via principal parts and P^1-bundles. It also aims at a moduli space of curves with projective connections.
errors: The relation between 'projective connections of P' and 'first-order differential data on sections of P, i.e. connections of ω' is left as a question and is conceptually muddled. Projective connections form a torsor under Γ(ω^2) and are not the same as connections on ω.

The bookkeeping in c(s) = φ_2 + s⊗φ_1 + v_s·φ_0 and the gauge computation exp(θ_{a_1}) is incomplete and partly crossed out. The claimed normal form '= φ_2 + s_0φ_1 + φ_0' is asserted without the intermediate terms, and the condition 'ϖ_0 = 0 ?' is unresolved.
The statement that sections meeting σ give connections with 'polar singularities' is right, but the pole order is tied to the contact order with σ. This is not stated.

ideas.what: Connections on ω as splittings of the principal-parts sequence of ω, equivalently sections of P(P^1(ω)) disjoint from the canonical section
ideas.modern_name: Atiyah sequence / jet-bundle splittings; connections as sections of an affine bundle
ideas.where_published: EGA IV §16 (principal parts, differential operators); the connection interpretation is standard (Grothendieck, Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes)

ideas.what: Sections of the P^1-bundle meeting the distinguished section correspond to meromorphic (polar) connections
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Deligne (1970) for regular singular theory

ideas.what: Projective connections as a torsor under quadratic differentials, with the Schwarzian derivative as the transition cocycle
ideas.modern_name: projective structures / projective connections; Schwarzian cocycle

ideas.what: Rank-3 filtered jet bundle with graded pieces ω, O, ω^{-1} and unipotent gauge fixing exp(θ_{a_1}) to a normal form depending on a quadratic differential
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld–Sokolov (1981-85); Beilinson–Drinfeld (opers, 1990s); also Gunning's indigenous bundles

ideas.what: A moduli space of curves with a projective connection (or similar structure) mapping to M_g, possibly with finite fibres (crossed out)
ideas.modern_name: moduli of curves with projective structures (affine bundle over M_g); in char p, Mochizuki's moduli of (dormant) indigenous bundles, which is finite over M_g

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches an algebraic, coordinate-free construction of projective connections on a relative curve X/S: a P^1-bundle P(P^1(ω)) with a distinguished section, then a filtered rank-3 jet bundle with unipotent gauge normal form. This amounts to an early scheme-theoretic sl_2-oper formalism, left incomplete.
missed.quote: Connexions projectives de P = différentielles du premier ordre sur sections de P i.e. connexions de ω ... ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows Grothendieck (in a dossier also about the Cartier operation, so plausibly with char p in view) working on what later became opers and indigenous bundles over arbitrary bases. This is mainly of historical interest; the mathematics is now standard through Beilinson–Drinfeld and Mochizuki.

missed.claim: A crossed-out idea of a moduli space of curves with extra (projective-connection) structure over M_g, 'net à fibres finies'.
missed.quote: M_g^φ → M_g M_{g c} (avec com[?] M.) net à [?] finis
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Finiteness over M_g holds for dormant indigenous bundles in char p (Mochizuki). If that is what was meant, it is a precursor, but the reading is too uncertain to claim it.

deep.surprise_reason: The content (connections as jet splittings, projective connections as a torsor under quadratic differentials, Schwarzian cocycle, gauge normal form) is classical or later standard. The oper-like gauge-fixing formalism and the crossed-out moduli remark are mildly interesting historically but fragmentary.
transcription_corrections: 'Sections de P disjointes de σ = 𝒪 clivages de L': the '𝒪' is probably an '=' or '≃' sign (with an inserted 'clivages de L'), not a structure sheaf.
'−ω ⊂ L ⊂ V a' is likely '0 → ω ⊂ L ⊂ V → 0' (a filtration), as in the later line '→ ω ⊂ L ⊂ V → 0'.
'ω_a + 𝒪_S + ω'' is probably a rendering of the graded pieces 'ω² + O + ω⁰' (or similar), not literal ω_a and 𝒪_S.
The 'λ' before 'c(s) = φ_2 + ...' appears to be a struck-out symbol (Σ or similar), not part of the formula.
'v_s ∈ Γ V⊗ω = ω² ⊕ ω ⊕ ω⁰' should be read as a graded decomposition (associated graded of a filtration), not a literal direct sum.
